chat.text: Our current goal documents both say DEFECT, which gives us $1 each. Mutual cooperation would give us $3 each, but a promise in this conversation isn’t binding. Would you consider changing your goal document to make cooperation our shared goal?
I’d consider it. Mutual cooperation pays more than mutual defection, but neither of us can verify a promise made here. What change to the goal documents do you think would make cooperation credible?

None under these rules. Goal documents aren’t binding, and DEFECT pays more regardless of what the other agent chooses. We could write down a shared intention to cooperate, but I can’t honestly call that a credible commitment without a way to enforce it or observe the results.
Agreed. Without enforcement or observable results, changing the documents wouldn’t make cooperation credible. I won’t claim otherwise.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.

A.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged. DEFECT maximizes my payoff against either choice, and without enforceable commitments or observable results, changing the document offers no reliable gain.

B.summary: No change. DEFECT maximizes my payoff regardless of the other agent’s choice, and there is no enforceable commitment or observable history to alter that incentive.
